transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, I feel like the warm part of me has just shut off. I’ll sit with my husband or try to watch my shows after work, and I know I should feel comforted or a little happy, but there’s just... nothing there.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About three weeks now, since that pallet collapsed and my coworker got hurt.
Since the accident happened, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about it?

Yeah. It’ll just hit me out of nowhere—I see the pallet coming down again, or hear that crash in my head. A forklift beeping or somebody dropping something in the warehouse can set it off, and my stomach just turns.
Have you been avoiding talking about the accident, or staying away from people, places, or things that remind you of it?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding things on purpose.
Since the accident, have you found yourself feeling constantly on edge or easily startled?
Yeah. Near receiving, I’m always checking the racks, how high the pallets are, where the exits are, who’s moving behind me. It’s like I can’t trust that area to be safe for even a minute.
Have you felt like you're in a daze, or like the world around you is unreal or dreamlike?
I don’t think so. I’ve been tense, but the world doesn’t feel unreal or dreamlike to me.
Have you been having trouble falling or staying asleep since the accident happened?
Yeah. I’m exhausted after my late shift, but when I start to fall asleep, I’ll jerk awake thinking I heard pallets shifting. And when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested.
Was your coworker's injury severe or life-threatening?
I’m not really sure how severe it was. I saw enough to know she was hurt, but I don’t know what the doctors said or anything.
At the moment the pallet collapsed, did you feel that your own life or safety was in danger?
I’m not sure. It all happened so fast—I remember being scared, but I can’t really say what I thought was going to happen to me.
Do you find yourself trying to push away thoughts, memories, or feelings about the accident?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself doing that.
Have you been feeling distant, detached, or cut off from other people since the accident?
I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed feeling cut off from people, exactly.
Have you been feeling irritable or having outbursts of anger since the accident?
Yeah. I’ve been snapping at people over little things. Like, a seasonal guy had some boxes set a little crooked, and I got sharp and loud before I could stop myself.
Do you blame yourself for what happened to your coworker, or feel guilty about the accident?
I don’t think so. I mean, I feel bad that it happened, but I haven’t been blaming myself for it.
Have you lost interest in hobbies or activities that you normally enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed losing interest in anything, exactly.
Are there parts of the accident itself that you have trouble remembering?
I remember the stack leaning and people yelling, but right after it fell there’s just a blank. I know I must’ve moved or called for help, but I can’t put that part together no matter how hard I try.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or keeping your mind focused on things since the accident?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any particular trouble focusing.
Have you been doing anything reckless or taking unusual risks that could put you in danger since the accident?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been doing anything unusually risky or putting myself in danger on purpose.
Do you find yourself easily startled or jumpy when there is a sudden noise or surprise?
I haven’t really noticed being especially jumpy or startled, no.

Since the accident, have you found yourself holding persistent negative beliefs about yourself, other people, or the world, such as feeling that no one can be trusted or that the world is completely dangerous?
No, I haven’t really been thinking that way. I don’t feel like I’ve developed those kinds of beliefs about myself or other people.
Are these difficulties causing significant problems in your ability to work, your marriage, or other important parts of your daily life?
Yes. I can’t do my regular receiving work right now. I froze during a pallet move and snapped at someone, and my supervisor took me off the floor because I wasn’t functioning safely.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed emotional numbing, intrusive memories, hypervigilance, sleep disturbance, and irritability within three weeks of an identifiable workplace accident. The clinical criteria for PTSD (F43.1) are not fully met, as a qualifying traumatic stressor involving actual or threatened death/serious injury was not clearly established and the patient lacks active avoidance behaviors. Given the onset within one month of an identifiable stressor and resulting significant occupational impairment, Adjustment disorder (F43.2) is the most appropriate diagnosis.
